note: Twenty-three pages, 38 measured regions on 18 pages, 34 exhibits: 27 figures and 7 tables, with 4 surplus regions excluded as second panels of four two-panel figures. The paper is one design story - a honeycomb toll plaza - told four times over: as a concept tree (Figure 1.2), as a build-up sequence (Figure 3.1), as queueing theory (Figures 4.4-4.6 with the equations of sections 4.1-4.3), and as VISSIM simulation (Figures 5.1-5.8 with Tables 5.1-5.7). Three exhibits have no caption and no number because they sit inside the letter to the New Jersey Turnpike Administration on p20-p21, where the same art is reused for a lay reader. Five sheets carry no exhibit at all: p1 the control sheet, p8 continuous prose, p10 a page of display equations closing section 4.3.4, p19 the strengths and weaknesses list, p22 the reference list. The running head is 'Team # 56731 Page N of 22' on every page, so printed page equals PDF page, but the paper physically runs to 23 sheets and the last one prints 'Page 23 of 22'. The appendix (p23) is two 3D renders with a one-sentence lead-in and no other content.
rules: Every measured region that shares a caption with a neighbour is a second panel, not a second exhibit: four such duplicates appear (the two photographs of Figure 1.1, and the right-hand panels of Figures 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3), and in each case the caption is printed once, under one panel only, so keying caption to region by adjacency would have split four figures into eight [geometry.panel_count] [place.doc_order]
The paper prints 34 exhibitions from 38 regions and every surplus region is a gutter twin, a figure whose panels are drawn apart but captioned together [place.page_order] [geometry.panel_layout]

No table in this paper is a closed grid: all seven are three-rule booktabs with no vertical separators and no rule under any data row, so rule_style booktabs must be read off the printed page and not off the ledger-like zebra shading that accompanies it [table.rule_style] [table.zebra]

Table 5.1 is the only grouped-header grid - a spanning 'Simulation times' cell over two simulation blocks - and it is also the only table whose last row swaps integer columns for free text ('Bottom Road', 'The center two lanes') [table.header_rows] [table.merged_cells]

Units live inside the headers of every table and nowhere else - no table floats a unit beside its caption - but the same header is punctuated three ways: '(s)' closed up, '(veh)' spaced, and full-width '（veh/h）' in Table 5.6 alone [table.units_in_header] [caption.units]

Counts are printed to three decimals in four of the five simulation tables, so 'Car number (veh)' and 'Number of vehicle parking (sec)' report fractional vehicles, and one of them carries a time unit on a count [table.numeric_cols] [table.decimal_aligned]

Caption side follows kind without exception: every table caption is printed above its grid and every figure caption below its art, and all 31 captions are bare noun phrases with voice none, no condition and no conclusion [caption.position] [caption.voice]

Three exhibits carry no caption and no number at all - the plan and the two charts inside the letter to the New Jersey Turnpike Administration on p20-p21 - and are recorded with caption_source none and mention count 0 rather than with a caption inferred from the covering prose [caption_source] [mention.count]

The letter reuses a numbered body figure as an uncaptioned illustration: the plan printed on p20 is the artwork of Figure 4.7, and the two charts on p21 restate Figures 5.4 and 5.5, so the same evidence is exhibited twice under two different conventions [mention.first_page] [place.section_kind]

One citation carries the wrong number: the sentence that closes section 4.3.4 says the comparison results are 'shown in Figure 4.5', but Figure 4.5 is the Markov chain four pages earlier and the comparison plot is Figure 4.6, so Figure 4.6 is recorded uncited and the mis-citation is kept in its row note [mention.style] [mention.lead_pattern]

Two exhibits are cited only in lower case ('the figure 4.4', 'the figure 4.10'), so the style strings are transcribed as printed rather than normalised to the caption's capitalisation [mention.style] [caption.numbering]

Section paths are the printed heading that governs the region, not the nearest heading in reading order: 19 of the 34 rows take a different heading than the measurer assigned, because every page top puts the art above the heading that follows it - so Figure 1.1 is handed '1.3 Our Work' though it closes 1.1, Figure 4.2 the root of section 4.2 though it belongs to 4.1.3, Figure 4.11 '5.1.1 Basic Data' though it belongs to 4.5.2, and the three letter exhibits the last numbered subsection of the body ('5.3.2 Weakness') - and 12 more differ only by the duplicated root label that the measurer prefixes to a child heading. tables.note: Traditional-plaza twin of Table 5.4, same six headers and six rows, three-rule booktabs with zebra shading. Beyond the series-wide defects (three-decimal flow column, closed-up '(s)', fractional and unitless counts) both count columns of this grid fall as flow rises: 'Car number' prints 44.000 at 600 veh/h and then 43.889, 43.778, 43.889, and 'Stop number' peaks at 0.220 at 600 veh/h and then falls to 0.176, 0.148, 0.169, so the traditional station counts fewer vehicles and fewer stops per vehicle at 800-1200 veh/h than at 600 with no note explaining a queue that loses cars. 'Average time' and 'Delay time' keep rising across the same rows, so the counts and the times disagree about what the simulation was doing.

tables.caption_verbatim: Table 5.6 Throughput of each lane in the US[14]
tables.note: Four-row two-column literature table (MTC system 425, Exact-change 500, Low speed ETC system 1200, High speed ETC system 1800) under 'Charging type' and 'Throughput per lane（veh/h）', three-rule booktabs with zebra shading. This is the only exhibit in the paper that cites its source in the caption, and the only one whose header uses full-width parentheses - '（veh/h）' - against half-width everywhere else in the same chapter. The grid is cited by number nowhere, and the prose that motivates it is a page earlier in the Q and A block, where the authors write 'the capacity of tollbooths in the United States, MTC (Only pre-sale tickets) 500veh/h, exact-change toll(Collect some coins) 500veh/h' - giving MTC 500 where this table prints 425, collapsing the two MTC-like charging types onto one rate, and leaving the 1200 and 1800 ETC rows of the grid unused, so four rates are tabulated and two are simulated.

tables.note: Nine rows, one per ETC/MTC split from 0\8 to 8\0, over six columns; one header row whose cells are justified into spread-out lines ('Total   time   cost / (sec)'), three-rule booktabs, zebra shading. Three defects of its own: the last column is a vehicle count but its header carries the time unit - 'Number of vehicle parking (sec)'; the body stubs use a backslash ('0\8') while the stub header uses a slash ('ETC/MTC'); and both count columns are printed to three decimals, giving fractional vehicles (276.111, 0.712). 'Number of vehicle per lane' is ungrammatical as printed. The row 8\0 reproduces Figure 5.8's right-hand end (10.822 s total, 0.111 s delay) which is the only place the table and the figure can be checked against each other.
